# Fixed-facet contraction with a reoptimized meeting point

This is a finite-menu upper certificate for an actual body variation. It does not assume that the displayed cap normals remain minimizing after the variation. The conclusion is conditional on an explicit support-function inequality; that inequality is not claimed from volume data alone.

Let A,K,B be planar convex bodies at integer bases -1,0,1 with (A+B)/2 subset K. Let y0 be in int K. Let v1,v2,v3 be nonzero spanning vectors with

    v1+v2+v3=0.

Write h_i=h_B(v_i). Suppose the three ACTUAL through-(0,y0) caps

    H_i={ (z,x):v_i.(x-y0)+(v_i.y0-h_i)z>=0 }                        (1)

have equal raw mass Q, and have proper positive-area cuts on both A and K. Their B traces are supporting faces of zero planar area. Put

    b_i=2v_i.y0-h_i,
    U_i=|A intersect {v_i.x>=b_i}|,
    sigma_Ai=H_1(A intersect {v_i.x=b_i})/||v_i||,
    sigma_Ki=H_1(K intersect {v_i.x=v_i.y0})/||v_i||,
    s_i=2sigma_Ai+sigma_Ki>0,
    lambda_i=1/s_i, Lambda=sum_i lambda_i.                            (2)

The division by ||v_i|| is essential when the normals are not unit. It makes sigma the derivative with respect to the actual scalar threshold.

Fix p in A and contract A by

    A_t=p+(1-t)(A-p), 0<=t<1.

Then actual midpoint compatibility persists because A_t subset A. For all sufficiently small t there are a C^1 meeting point y(t) in int K, y(0)=y0, and a common cap budget q(t), q(0)=Q, such that the three caps obtained from (1) by replacing y0 by y(t) all have mass q(t) on A_t,K,B. They cover the entire middle fiber. In particular the true maximum mixed depth for the new body is at most

    max{(1-t)^2 m_A,m_B,q(t)},                                       (3)

where m_A,m_B are the ordinary maximum depths of A,B. Moreover

    q'(0)=-Lbar(p),
    Lbar(p)=[sum_i lambda_i L_i(p)]/Lambda,
    L_i(p)=2U_i+(b_i-v_i.p)sigma_Ai.                                 (4)

The best first-order loss among these actual contractions is attained and equals

    max_(p in A) Lbar(p)
      =[2sum_i lambda_i U_i+sum_i lambda_i b_i sigma_Ai
          +h_A(-sum_i lambda_i sigma_Ai v_i)]/Lambda.                (5)

## Proof of the actual finite-menu certificate

For arbitrary y near y0, retain the fixed normals and B-support thresholds. Their B contributions stay exactly zero and their other contributions are

    F_i(y,t)=|K intersect {v_i.x>=v_i.y}|
        +|A_t intersect {v_i.x>=2v_i.y-h_i}|.                         (6)

All involved cuts remain proper in a neighborhood. A planar convex body's section-length function is continuous at every threshold strictly between its support extremes: it is a finite concave function there (equivalently apply the elementary one-dimensional Brunn--Minkowski inequality to sections). Thus its cap-area function is C^1 there, with derivative minus section length divided by normal length. Under homothety of A, the same assertion holds jointly for y,t; its exact pulled-back threshold and positive area multiplier give this directly. Consequently

    grad_y F_i(y0,0)=-s_i v_i.

The three equations F_i(y,t)=q have a nonsingular derivative in (y,q). If -s_i v_i.delta_y-delta_q=0 for every i, multiply by 1/s_i and sum. Since sum v_i=0, this gives delta_q=0, and then the spanning property gives delta_y=0. The C^1 implicit-function theorem proves the asserted C^1 path. If the bodies have smoother proper-section data, the path has the corresponding smoothness; no greater regularity is needed for (4). No smoothness beyond C^1 is asserted under the stated convex-body hypotheses.

At the meeting point, the three middle halfspaces cover all of R^2, since all v_i.(x-y) cannot be negative when their sum is zero. Hence for every point of the middle fiber one of the actual ambient caps contains it and has budget q(t). This proves its optimized depth upper bound without any assertion that these caps remain critical, or that every other normal has a gap. Endpoint fiber maxima equal their ordinary maxima by finite integer-tilt isolation, so (3) follows.

The homothety formula for the A cap at a fixed threshold b_i is

    (1-t)^2 |A intersect
       {v_i.x>=(b_i-t v_i.p)/(1-t)}|.

Differentiation at zero gives its derivative -2U_i-(b_i-v_i.p)sigma_Ai=-L_i(p). Differentiating the equal-budget equations yields

    q'(0)=-s_i v_i.y'(0)-L_i(p).

Multiplication by lambda_i and summation eliminates the moving meeting point exactly, proving (4). Finally Lbar is affine and continuous in p; A is compact. Minimizing p dot sum lambda sigma_A v over A is the negative support value in (5), proving attainment and the formula. Every L_i(p) is nonnegative because the contraction nests inside A; this fact alone supplies no quantitative lower bound for the weighted average.

## Exact normalized-descent criterion and source-switch limitation

Assume in addition that Q is the ORIGINAL true globally maximal raw depth, and that

    m_A<Q, m_B<Q.

Then the endpoint terms in (3) remain strictly below q(t) for all sufficiently small t. Let M=|A|+|K|+|B| and a=|A|. Since M'(0)=-2a, (3)--(4) imply strict decrease of the true optimized normalized depth whenever

    Lbar(p)>2a Q/M.                                                  (7)

Indeed the derivative of the upper certificate q(t)/M(t), which equals the original depth at t=0, is [-M Lbar(p)+2aQ]/M^2<0. Thus this is an actual descent even if the new true depth is smaller than the certificate. The deformed centers need not be identified further.

Under a hypothetical planar n=1 below-target premise Q/M<Gamma_2/2=2/9, the explicit sufficient test is

    max_p Lbar(p)>=Gamma_2 a=4a/9.                                  (8)

In the canonical normalization y0=0 and h_i=1, equation (5) becomes

    [2sum lambda_i U_i-sum lambda_i sigma_Ai
       +h_A(-sum lambda_i sigma_Ai v_i)]/Lambda.                     (9)

No proof that (9) always meets (8) is asserted. The section, support and criticality data must come from the SAME actual A,K,B; they are not independent scalar variables. Also the strict endpoint gaps cannot be dropped: if m_B=Q, shrinking A while leaving B fixed can increase the normalized value of that competing endpoint. The exact reflected-containment example in `candidate 02c6510b145c2710` displays this source switch and tracks it explicitly.

## A proved section-balance sufficient condition

The three fixed A halfspaces in (2) cover the entire plane. Indeed

    sum_i b_i=-sum_i h_B(v_i)<0.

The strict inequality follows by choosing an interior point of B: every support value is strictly larger than its value there, and the v_i sum to zero. If all three A inequalities failed at a point, summation would give 0<sum b_i<0. For the nested contraction A_t subset A, the removed A-cap volume is exactly the measure of the shell A minus A_t in that fixed halfspace. Coverage therefore gives

    sum_i [U_i-|A_t intersect {v_i.x>=b_i}|] >= a-|A_t|.

Divide by t and let t decrease to zero. Formula (4) proves, for EVERY p in A,

    sum_i L_i(p)>=2a.                                                (10)

Since each L_i(p)>=0, it follows that

    Lbar(p)>=2a (min_i lambda_i)/Lambda.                              (11)

Thus the actual below-target contraction descent criterion is satisfied whenever

    min_i lambda_i/Lambda >= 2/9.                                   (12)

A convenient, explicitly stronger section condition is

    max_i s_i/min_i s_i <=7/4,   s_i=2sigma_Ai+sigma_Ki.               (13)

In fact the same ratio bounds max lambda/min lambda, and
min lambda/Lambda>=1/[1+2(max lambda/min lambda)]>=2/9. Under the original strict endpoint gaps, (12) or (13) and Q/M<2/9 yield an actual strict normalized-depth descent, with no persistence assumption for critical normals.

There is also a rigorous support-sensitive improvement of (11). For any index j, choose p to maximize L_j. Then

    max_p Lbar(p) >=
      [2a lambda_min+(lambda_j-lambda_min) L_j^max]/Lambda,
    L_j^max=2U_j+[b_j+h_A(-v_j)]sigma_Aj.                             (14)

This uses (10), nonnegativity of all losses, and the actual support point attaining the displayed maximum. Taking the maximum over j keeps the same actual A. Equation (14) can strengthen the balance test when a cap with large weight has a large removable shell. No assertion that (12), (13), or (14)'s sufficient numerical threshold follows automatically from a bad-source premise is made.

## Actual missing corners improve the weighted shell credit

The following exact improvement was independently supplied by Defect Transport. In the canonical normalization b_i=-1, define the ACTUAL unique-capture regions

    R_i=A intersect intersection_(j!=i){v_j.x<-1},
    E={i:R_i is empty}.

A point with only cap i captured must belong to R_i, so every point of A has weighted capture load at least

    tau=min( {lambda_i:i not in E}
                  union {lambda_i+lambda_j:i!=j} ).                 (15)

The minimum over an absent singleton list is simply omitted. There are always pair sums. Triple capture has no smaller weight than a pair, because all weights are positive. The same lower bound holds pointwise on every actual removed shell A minus A_t. Integration and differentiation give, for every p in A,

    sum_i lambda_i L_i(p)>=2a tau,
    Lbar(p)>=2a tau/Lambda.                                         (16)

Thus tau/Lambda>=2/9 is another explicit sufficient condition for the below-target strict descent, with the same endpoint-gap requirements. If the smallest-weight unique-capture region is absent, tau is at least the second-smallest weight. If all unique-capture regions are absent, tau is the sum of the two smallest weights. These are actual geometric incidences of one fixed A, not a freely chosen scalar profile. The inequality is also valid when an R_i is merely area-null, by ignoring its null subset in the shell integral. For strict region emptiness no null-set qualification is needed.

## A tied large endpoint: an exact two-rate test

The following extension retains a possible competing B source instead of assuming its gap. Assume Q is the original true global maximum, m_A<Q, and m_B=Q. Write k=|K|, b=|B|, a=|A|, M=a+k+b, r=Q/M. Choose p in A, q in B and rates u,v>=0, not both zero. Contract A,B at rates u,v while keeping K fixed:

    A_t=p+(1-ut)(A-p), B_t=q+(1-vt)(B-q).

For all sufficiently small t these are positive bodies nested in A,B, so compatibility persists. The B support value changes exactly as

    h_(B_t)(v_i)=h_i-vt(h_i-v_i.q).

Retain the same normals in (6) and replace h_i there by this actual new support value. The equal-menu implicit-function argument is unchanged. Its common budget satisfies

    q_menu'(0)=-u Lbar(p)-v Jbar(q),
    Jbar(q)=[sum_i lambda_i sigma_Ai(h_i-v_i.q)]/Lambda>=0.           (17)

The extra loss comes from the upward change of the A threshold when the opposite supporting B facet moves inward. It is not a first-order B captured volume, which remains exactly zero. The maximum of Jbar is attained, with

    Jbar_max=[sum_i lambda_i sigma_Ai h_i+h_B(-V)]/Lambda,
    V=sum_i lambda_i sigma_Ai v_i.                                  (18)

The true new global maximum is bounded by the maximum of this menu budget and the two exact endpoint ordinary maxima (1-ut)^2 m_A, (1-vt)^2 Q. The A term stays separated. Since M'(0)=-2(au+bv), strict decrease of both remaining normalized upper bounds is certified by

    u Lbar(p)+v Jbar(q)>2r(au+bv),
    Qv>r(au+bv).                                                     (19)

These are complete first-order tests for this specified two-rate upper certificate, not necessary conditions for all possible body deformations.

For u>0 put t_ratio=v/u. The second inequality is exactly

    t_ratio>a/(a+k).

Let L=Lbar(p), J=Jbar(q). If J>2rb, taking a sufficiently large t_ratio gives both inequalities. If J<=2rb, existence of an admissible t_ratio is equivalent to

    (a+k)L+aJ>2aQ.                                                   (20)

Indeed the first inequality is (L-2ra)+t_ratio(J-2rb)>0; with a nonpositive slope its supremum on the strictly admissible interval is its value at the left endpoint, which must be strictly positive. This is exactly (20). For a zero slope the same strict test applies. If J>2rb, B-only contraction u=0 also works. Because the coefficients of L,J in (19) are nonnegative, their independently attained support maxima (5),(18) may be used simultaneously by choosing the corresponding two actual contraction centers.

This extension prevents silently ignoring a tied endpoint. It also shows why the weaker one-endpoint loss threshold need not suffice at a source switch: when J is small, (20) asks for a larger A loss. No lower bound sufficient for (20) is inferred from missing corners or small a alone.
